calling it a perusal of his dream --
where it most definitely, certainly, absolutely, conspiratorially, does not want to be --
him hoarding its freedom.
The shadiest characters can make their shadow
from a spotlight.
To the world, he’s the uncle in the corner
whose articulation is vulgar, but not avuncular,
a whodunit of soul’s murder,
of one who does not own for himself

title: Super Mario; Or, Everything I Needed to Learn About Relationships
publication: Published in Mithila in 2019 /Republished in Corncrake in 2026
body: All relationships can be linked to Super Mario
(who is you -- implicitly an immigrant,
only ever seen as a stereotype
to those of the “kingdom,”
and all your friends are toads
and your clothes are never in style but styled old)
Mushrooms,
Basically it’s what you scrap by with eating,
On a diet of veggies to look good,
AND BULK UP,
While you kill yourself (sans extra lives)
To save the princess, which --
is really like smashing your head
against a brick wall…literally,
and expecting some reward.
During the process of romantic pursuit you grow up,
and are made to feel so small,
try on different looks,
become a tanuki,
that shapeshifter who can be anything else possibly,
to fool people because
we’re all fools in love.
(don’t forget how that raccoon plays his testicles in repeated rhythms…)
So you,
a blue-collar man,
with a body that maps the march of time,
has the stamp of capitalism
just moves forward.
But you try,
you haven’t lost yet,
but it’s getting there
you sludge through shit
one pipe after another
through the sewers of life
To find the girl of your dreams
(and you’re not even entirely sure why)
who is with some other man
a real lizard, or something.
(P.S. Physical confrontation with masculinity that’s only toxic when it’s not for the benefit of another).
Your journey will always take you into
another world,
but for aught because
always,
always, your princess is always in another castle.

title: Synthetic water; or Plan B (a satire…I hope)
publication: Published in Glass Gates Publishing, Kreatif in 2026
body: Should our fears become manifest –
and that manifestation be absence: namely, our water sipped from the earth as if from a straw of God’s, leaving nothing but the tragic sight of empty pools.
A plan (which is to say plan B) for what we can do afterwards with the best of our abilities: namely, to make and bottle a corporate substitute: Synthetic Water.
“Less effort.”
“More waste.”

Those can be the taglines, which we could also profligate like a chant, as we bottle and market, bottle and market, bottle and market (like a train chugging along) the product -- spread it over the earth, probably not seventy percent of it excepting spreading the name. People will know our product not just through the taste, but through its marketing, which inferior water never had.
You’ll know it’s knock-
off water from that corporate logo,
which will be estimated at a value of
something beyond human life.

Disclaimer: it will be less efficient than real water and probably will not hydrate the body, and even if it did hydrate the body, it might contain heavy metals that we will say are not proven to be dangerous --
But it will be certified and get tax breaks.
It will not quench thirst,
but it will be consumable.

In fact, it will be superior to water in that you will always crave more and therefore will lead to an endless stream of demand – pun intended. In fact, it will be ultra-consumable.  The market can be cornered so much that the earth will be square again – downright Pythagorean in all its limits.
For should the planet die,
our bank accounts won’t.

title: ‘Teh’
publication: Published in WINK in 2018 / Republished in The Lake around 2018 / Republished in Galway Review in 2026
body: E’ry time I type up a poem
Of moored and sandy thoughts
My fingers dance on loan
And renegades they be,
type a peculiar word –‘teh’
From where is this word
Of homeward thoughts?
to free said convicts
from out their prison stick.
Is a sign of my aging years
of arthritic fingers stumbling
in the Ben Hur of typists,
whose Roman numerals are bloated.
Or is it born of the unconscious --
in that loom of the mind,
where weaves an Arachne able,
entangling thoughts in their way.
Is it something to be deciphered --
a code (like most of poetry)
to bury in a ‘t’ the crossword
title, beyond letters hyetal?
Might it be some slang,
written on a slant,
to boorish hours
of morning all alone.
Yet in this monstrosity
something touches my soul –
not only the words we teach,
but even ‘teh’ bloated things
we mispronounce.

title: Thanksgiving
publication: Published in Pennsylvania Literary Journal in 2018
body: I don’t think things through --
“I love you.”
The last month’s hypocrisy
is now mimicked in my mouth--
the weather
recalled in my mind like a trauma,
a season unseasoned in its fickleness,
a Baltic habit coming out once again…
well, at least I tried.
The threat of snow flurries
didn’t need to be stated.
And the kiddos laughed outside
like fairies dancing on broken glass.
We walked along houses,
strewn like dirty dishes along a sink,
hosting what will not be the talk of tomorrow.
I only know what is the least present,
stretched along a fathomless mind.
And in the dime of the eye,
I see the world as a duplicate self --
an ambush of shadows,
an ambush of copies,
an ambush of the little things,
an ambush of my very own voice --
to speak but of itself
but only to matter in the crook of another’s ear.
Why ask where we were going?
“Was it to be that road less trod on?” You said.
I said back, “I don’t want to know.”
(hell, I don’t even know the road’s name),
and now my spirit’s diagonal.
To enter
into the humid air of the house:
the wind’s heavy-hanging
scrotum hits the face,
and a familial swarm mills about
like unpaid proletariats.
We heated the bird,
but not the conversation --
and were hugged by the many doors: our table, our dinner…
The crowd was possessed by the holidays --
but we were already taken.
We couldn’t forget that outside
all the din was actually true.
Rape the body of the earth.
Rape the bodies that hoist up the earth --
pillage, violate, obfuscate it all
(I sigh)
until the father was proven right
…until the disrespect is overloaded to the level of the linguistic
…until I drown in a spew of synonyms.
All accurate.
None emotional.
This is what we’re thankful for,
so the only thing I could do was worship
my body spread out.
The only thing that mattered
was how much the physical was
mimicking my analogies.
I had put the pencil to my head
in a suicidal motion,
brought it down with a crash on the paper.
My oh my -- let the word die,
drowned in a sea of white lies.
So I travel on foot to your heart --
my shoes licking the pavement --
to wherever I housed my memories,
a place as empty as this house is full,
ever looking for something there,
ever stuck in the hallways of yearbook,
ever lost in the maze thereof,
ever waiting for the coming dawn,
but never the chosen one.
The sun
lit only the surfaces of things;
more so, it lit only the surfaces
that I have touched.
I drew a rough draft of God,
discovering more of your face --
every time I look at it --
in every line I follow with an imprisoned eye,
studying whatever I thought I saw
balder and bolder.
Our mittens were cuffs in the cold November day,
saying we never had to leave
...but that’s not what we actually believe.
What they thought were their morals were disgusting.
What the day represented was two-faced,
yet we shouted across the lawn
“I am yours,”
like some alleged movie cliché.
I want to make language dance like a wanton girl
as seen in the eyes of a lonely prude.
I want my analogies to dance around the world
on the lips of any brief lover.
But it wouldn’t show.
It would only tell a cardinal sin
(“Haha,” we’d say -- how funny is it
that we only remember the seven sins?)
But it only came out:
“I love you.”
See, I always said I was a fool.

title: That Poem, This Poem
publication: Published in Orenaug Mountain Poetry in 2019
body: Oh yes, that poem, which was something like three words
that I can’t pronounce,
those three words I can’t say
and so get stuck over me,
hanging on a jacket or its sleeve
but never ne’er me.
That poem - -
perhaps it’s only the one who never heard those words
who would mock that poem.
Perhaps it is he who smolders papers
with the friction of getting tongue-tied who despises it.
That poem, which I read first to me,
and then recited to you.
That poem, with the lame phrase:
“I love you.”
So this poem can be for him,
who mocks that poem
and let him hear its simple phrase
redone anon:
to you -- I love.

title: A Christmas Card from Kyiv
body: The bombs are dropping all around,
but hey, glad everybody’s great --

title: The City in the Valley; Or, the Upside-Down Frown
publication: Published in Zombie Logic Review in 2013-2018
body: My eight minds shine on the hollowed dark sun,
Pushing me down to a tentacled ton.
A Leviathan green swallows me whole.
In a pit of nothing, no sleep, my toll.
I spiral down into darkness spread full:
E’ermore, E’ermore - to answer with a snore
The tapping, rapping of one with no role,
On this dusty casket’s creaking old floor
The blight keys of Sunday’s paramour’s wiles
Forever locked within fictional smiles.
Killers of another circle will write
A page on the sky’s black canvas tonight.
Why wish upon that dark, faded star’s shore
(Once bright) if I have no soul anymore?

title: The Dead
body: Their faces are the same --
because they were a company
outfit.
Dressed to the ‘T’
to be placed in a mausoleum
shrine,
with primped sleeves
and brushed fabric.
For the new-age dead
are just as uniform
as every box on (and off)
the wall-calendar.
My feet walked forward
Before I took a step – all steps
Laid out in a Gantt chart
marching down aisles,
as slowly as the rising
of the weekday sun.
The smiles you see are rated
higher than the ties,
which hung those sinners of the self.
And in this perpetual prison
with one door off,
holding within sweating flesh.
I sat within these three-walls
poorer for the money
I made:
savoir vivre fit on a PowerPoint,
a bulleted list to shoot down any –
hope, future, love, life…
And anon, no more – a post-it
eulogy.  Not much said
for the identical dead.
The reports were stacked onto mounds,
stapled,
filed, meant to be shred.
But no one did the same
for the pitiful
dead.

title: The Definition of Irony
body: “Jump, jump,” they shouted,
And the shout became a howl.
Like the Romans shouting
A mixed cadence of “Barritus,”
Keeping time to the sun’s passage in the sky
The crowd came
To see the splat, to see the goo
Like an eggy breakfast on a Sunday afternoon,
And all these thoughts don’t add up right
But hate flies from lips like a caged bird.
There were kids down there, goddammit.
(he didn’t know why people squished that word together as they did --
which seemed like the greatest sacrilege,
a portmanteau to combine “god” and “dammit”
without a break.
Hell, even “death row” has a break in it.)
“Goddammit.”  He said.
Freefalling ethics with no safety net
(to speak of)
For oddity is taboo….
So he stood at a height of loneliness from greater depths --
Upon a clock tower as high as the hour.
The kid (a kid in his problems and adult in all else)
Looked down at the -- ever growing.
What?
Were they people from this height?
Were they people this far from his plight?
He heard these chants before:
“Cut it up and down,” they said, “not lengthwise,” in their know-it-all-ism.
(they liked to stop and look at car wrecks)
(but never the car)
The tale of the masses is old
Dulled in the tar of history.
We can say nothing new about them,
So we say nothing at all.
They wanted him dead.
Didn’t they?
This man, he stood, this man he would…
This man he jeered, this man he cheered.
But all of them wanted him to fall
--or rather they wanted him to jump into his stationary fall.
“Why was he here?” was what the nicer ones would ask.
But only in soundbite,
without empathy, but without jeer.
They wondered how many stories
He had underneath him
--That would only support the fall.
(Because only The Fall could come from stories).
The crowd below looked up
He above looked down.
The chant continued and continued…
With his vertigo thoughts
He thought the thoughts he wasn’t having.
He thought the thoughts his thoughts would think.
“Jump, Jump, Jump!”
It could have been written a thousand times.
And on the precipice he thought how ironic would it be
(knowing he would be chided this is not irony)
To turn the world upside down:
With the crowd above and him below.
So he took out from his jacket
What he called his friend.
And let the lead fall as it would.
But!
Even if poems are meant to be beautiful.
Why are awful subjects dressed in tuxes?
The tragedian could not really cry
That’s why he wore masks to hide.
But those below; they could not hide.
From a bullet like a butterfly.
Not only was it the most ironic thing of all,
It was the funniest thing he ever saw.

title: The Dreamer
body: What can a dreamer ever be
If that dreamer do be me?
For what to do when I see you
Lying next to me?
When we lie entwined and aligned,
Then my mind can never find
If what I gleam is but a dream
Or of a waked mind
Since in yourself I know perfection,
With absolutely no exception,
Then in this late nocturnal fete
Dreams and reality do conflate.

title: The Grand Illusion
publication: Published in Pennsylvania Literary Journal in 2018
body: Broken triggers on a leash held short,
Still tug out of our burnt hands.
Only the people seen in the cityscape,
even exist to the boss,
who plays these foosball tables uncouthly.
We’re suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder
with straw dolls.
Somewhere in the world lies a conglomeration
Of all things bet and won.
But I don’t think this qualifies for it.
And I really don’t think the tone that was taken
was appropriate for corporate humor.
This is an Orwell novel translated into Esperanto --
with footnotes.
The world’s Order is ‘senating’ is,
writing a thousand novels where nothing fucking happens.
Typing them up with monkey fingers,
we fell asleep in the middle of a theory.
It’s a testament to the philosophy of roulette,
to the impossibility of nothing yet.

title: The Fool and the Lion
body: Pinwheel
Of
Fortune…on a broken stand.
The turn can e’er hit ‘Happy’
“Thank God for poor times,”
Says the Fool of a Thousand Grins -
For its revolutions
Puts a discount on possible words.
Do I need to tell you this
Is a love poem?

title: The Mystery of Orpheus
body: Please --
Advise me how to wake up
(possibly in the morning)
How is it done (with skill or caution)?
I've searched in stale literature,
possibly packed with asbestos,
to find some stolid emotions.
Yawns are like clay --
molded with the cauliflowered hand of time
and not rated on a growing Likert scale --
But rising more awkwardly like a bird with wings clipped.
And the status-quo is already a sing-song relic,
Of what you call the “now.”
And "Hold on" is but an island,
navigating a 'what' in full rotation
(and the rest is black).
So in this bed:
I don’t know how to get up.
there's metaphorical cocaine on a nose protruding --
it's Pinocchio in a whirlpool of know-it-allism,
wishing it all could be real.

title: The Perception of my Own Grave
body: The perception of my own grave
Is always a long thought.
Death becomes pictorial,
Held by the thistled frame of tall grass.
This mountain at a’ given distance
All the more clear becomes
When the artist’s jiggling hand
Drops the coarse brush in art’s depiction.
It seems a shame that anything
But weeds should form this shroud.
Yet th’ joke’s calling this plot mine
When worms form my makeshift diadem

title: The Sins
body: Nobody ate, the sins.
mal du siècle, I thought
only in fifteen lines at least.
Does that make sense?
Oh well, if not – I think sometimes of my verse
as being a scourge upon nouns.
But what does it matter if it matters –
aren’t we always-already assuming
Meaning
In our talks
of meaning?  In that sense, the sin
(The Sin) could not have been a sin
If knowledge and meaning determined it
before there was
Knowledge and meaning.
Apples, nobody ate
tumbled down the gullet to satisfy a need
before it grew,
Grew with malicious roots to make beauty
unattainable…and move those roots
to the mind.
And choking
stops the stream of words that may come
mercifully.
Nobody ate.

title: Therapy
body: I’m listening for the solid echo
Of a love-word not spoken even once

title: This is not a poem II
publication: Published in Modern Literature in 2018 / Republished in Agony Opera in around 2018
body: Ceci n'est pas une –
I don’t speak French,
I’m not even casually acquainted with it really, so it may
Be.
Full stop.
More so, I don’t smoke --
said the man
to the
man,				(himself)
But I do know how to lie.
This godwottery will only grow,
can ever know
the treachery of life.

title: This poem will hit on you
publication: Published in Knot Magazine in 2018 / Republished in Ginosko in 2026
body: This poem will hit on you,
send an ebonite word to
wink and *smack* -- into your
lips, only to bounce back
to me,  snuggling closely.
To be “being,” this poem
will hit on you with a kindness:
It’s its Fach  --
stumbling back into
flirtatious reveries like oceanic tides.
It’s rafty (cold or bleak); it is
most writings you see
today.  And if beauty of words
could make you come…
to your senses, then --
Then this poem will hit on you--
you, who is not me.
Why would you keep yourself
away from everyone –
the everyman, the other other?
It will hit on you
when your bodice takes flight,
from off your body running,
when your body croons
erected.
And I scribble down a mantra
so profound,
but unfortunately one I can’t read
the next morning -- but I will ask you
what it means.
This poem will hit on you,
But -- but it won’t tell you what it wants.
It’d rather look at you through a prism
to see you in dots,
and use this broken image to --you know.

title: Three Oddest Words
publication: Published in UnLost in 2019 / Republished in Ginosko in 2026
body: I destroy words even as I speak them
My lips disassembling them outright:
Future – the first syllable already
In the past by the time it manifests.
Silence -- decimated by a’ wreckingball
Of a consonants spoken over the teeth.
Nothing – a poor word betraying itself
On my lip’s a priori insistence.

title: To Bowie A poem about reflecting in reverence to Bowie, with at least ten allusions to him (not readily obvious) that is meant to be read through the codex of those allusions.
publication: Published in Door is a Jar in 2019
body: ...and your dreams are so close to your face
that they gave you a black eye.
(We sat down on the couch and kept falling,
looking for Major Tom – our drinks rye).
The glam stars hung loosely above us,
where man made a cliché of god’s beauty,
so turn the record on its spindle
but only if its rotation is a rebellious duty.
Sitting, we passed upon the stairs
to meet a pretty thing, who only
gingerbreaded up her eyes, sans gaze,
so that we existed together lonely.
We died with our mouths open
from the memory of a free will,
before the hologramic machine
took our ashes and made our fame kill.
Let’s soar my friend to the greatest heights
with a wink and a satanic grin.
How sad if the planets above didn’t dance
with beautiful and feigned indifference.

title: Our Dream’s on a Stroll (To M- )
body: Out on a porch
Somewhere left of tomorrow
The Birds sang all around us.
Once I thought I was born an analogy,
So I sang words straight out of a can.
But for us now, the wait is over -
I’m still holding you.
A slogan: ‘Stroll with a heel-to-toe step:
The World is only as big as a mind.’
And now the world is just a reflection
Of your smile.
Our hands formed a Mobius strip
As rain egged
The seconds on
While you trickled into me.
Who said that? You asked.
Fitting an ocean
Between empty bed sheets,
Our bodies were like an Impressionist painting,
And my words came out a blur. And the things I want to say
Are the things I think you know:
I wanted to read you the history book of the ego
But I looked in your eyes and got lost
In some familiar place.
Then, like when a mirror’s too shy to see itself
Thought carried thought
As my lips were silenced on your neck.
But you understood it all
Here’s the truth:
I’m only a poet
When I think of you.

title: To My Wife - With A Copy Of My Poems
body: I can write no stately proem
As a prelude to my lay;
From a poet to a poem
I would dare to say.
For if of these fallen petals
One to you seem fair,
Love will waft it till it settles
On your hair.
And when wind and winter harden
All the loveless land,
It will whisper of the garden,
You will understand.

title: To Steal a Cento
body: She dwelt among the untrodden ways.
In the deserted, moon-blanched street,
They came in a ramshackle tub.
Children of the future age,
You will not emerge from subterranean time.
Thus I complain, in piteous strain,
O wake in me in my house in the mud
Or influence, chide or cheer the drooping stage
Upon the Muses' anvil; turn the same.
Some thrice three years: they went and came,
It may be that the gulfs will wash us down:
"He saw you, then? What did he do? Did he frown?"
The catch-cries of the clown, was born to wear a crown.
Ye know on earth, and all ye need to know
And Uniforms of snow
Set me where as the sun doth parch the green.
Waves that warble twitteringly,
And moulded in colossal calm
Tell me not, in mournful numbers.
This said, I am thine—and so its ink has paled.

title: To think of love as a word
publication: Published in Visions with Voices in 2018
body: And
I just stepped into her house
on the threshold of the future --
a nyaff in a mind of whiskey,
but anent nothing but our sighs.
And
a haunt of an hollowed spoon
can bring her tears to my mouth
where I can drink of those bitters
to the future sins within us both.
And
her eyes fluttered in an endless circle
as I stood firmly in the now:
so old I can’t remember my first kiss;
so young I can’t remember my last.
And
I only learned the word
“nacreous” to steal sympathy
From those very eyes
For what you call “always.”

title: Tomorrow Didn’t Matter
body: Tomorrow didn’t matter, except it kept arriving.
But it would never come on time.
I thought it rude of it, when I was so dour –
But perhaps that’s only my opinion sour.
Time kept coming like an uninvited guest –
Showing up when I didn’t want it,
And hospitality held me a hostage unfree–
Like a Hamadryad in its tree.
Then yet again, I’m an accoucheur
For yet another dawn’s birth --
My responsibility, growing asunder,
Has ever been my perennial blunder.
For thinking of time moving on is quite specious
Because tomorrow itself never changes,
A rough draft, in the mind ever the same thing,
At once a hope and yet unseen.

title: Took a Fire and Stuck it in an Envelope
body: Took a fire and stuck it in an envelope --
twas nobody’s fault but my own.
Sent it to the beadle of the local church,
and it was used to prop up the whole foundation.
Took a mannequin out to dinner,
and everything went just fine:
the conversation was predictable,
which made it easy to have again.
But oh, I licked the roof of my mouth
and tried to clear the words stuck up there,
but the bitter world turned its back
into the blankness of a word.
It turned its back on the
dark fount of the unspoken.
It turned its back on the lack of meetings done round
(just like it does everyday).
Saw a man strung between an open space,
talking through a pepper face.
His spittle carried more meaning than his vowels,
which were hot off the trail of a penny’s worth.
The man got sucked up a fireplace,
and as he tried to cut his arms off --
under a skeptic’s tunic long enough to drape the world,
everything seemed false all around.
Now they know how to pigeon-hole
themselves in a wide open field.
Now they know how what it’s like
to sit and languish in Nowheresville.

title: Tragic Young Love
body: Her hips had a certain shy rotation
In a bathtub of utter disrepair
For in the realm of perjury’s nation
Oath’s are downtrodden in a’ blister’s pained snare.
Spying a’ man blessed with the throw of a die,
As too-blue tussles hung below her eye
Her sullen gaze had flown by the wayside.
Her sighs, she mangled with sudden deride,
And from her lips passed a’ vial o’ roses quick
To shackle young thoughts with manacles thick -
Chains of a sweetness seldom seen or smelled
A lycanthropy o’ Diana’s fire quelled.
So to the faucet o’ vows spoke in young rhyme
At least truth can be: they meant it at th’ time.

title: Uncle Martin’s Thrift and Discount
body: Winter winds can only tell lies
Those charlatans of haughtily
Refined words.  Tell them to kiss
The sunrise and I and you and
Anyone who surmises a natural
Riddle translated from Helvetica
Will eat the tinniest words you’ve
Never Seen.  But alas, allow
That along alighted fields
Of the most natural study
That was ever rehashed:
Modern comes again.

title: Unseen Someone
publication: Published in Visions with Voices in 2018
body: It’s just another night --
out on the patio of the moon
With my hands cradling each other
and the lilies all in bloom
While my shadow’s too shy
to stand next to me.
In that brief moment,
cut from that shrinking world of our own
We sold all that we knew,
even the ‘what’ that constituted it all.
I hid behind my face,
knowing you would come too soon.
Put a helmet on my opinion,
and threw down the stairs like a bowling ball.
And on my bedroom walls
pin-ups of my favorite philosophy,
But only ever in snippets
and only ever washed in white.
I mourn the years before I learned how to misbehave.
It’s not my fault I couldn’t see into the past,
And I'm waiting for someone unseen,
from out the only book I ever wrote.
And I’m waiting for someone unmet,
only sketched out in minor rote.

title: Untitled #50
body: Ever about The The --
their small hands shook the sky
until the nails
holding it up, fell down --
glittering like the twinkle in her kohl eye.
His eye --
like the Chaurapanchasika,
wandered like a cow on a
path
not trodden.  It bathed in a pool of light --
He, the face of can’t.
It said:
“Life is a pencil sharpener,
before the lead recklessly crashes onto the page,”
a bean curd
a spice to stick in the curd
a motion to make the curd more palatable --
Her eye –
like a wilted champak flower
wandered down to leave
the gods.  It only exists in short
separations.
“Oh, recklessness of I,”
mouths of the country said --
to drink from her mouth --
she, with a hundred flatteries so heavy
they destroy the meaning of words
even now
What’s to say is said,
is said:
Words entangled his heart in a snare, like
Kashmir.

title: Untitled
body: I want to break the morning in two
And give both sides equal love,
Erect a wrought iron gate against the sunshine -
That shower of light slowly trickling to my eye,
Fill up humanity like a balloon
To meet the horse-drawn carriage of tomorrow’s boon.
I took an insurance policy out on the sun,
So bury that horse in the ground.
For in the margin of the horizon,
Lies the shadow of your face,
Moving twenty-five thousand miles in pace
To wind up in the bulky same place.
Soldiers of something hard-to-speak
Hide in a fortress of bed-sheets
And pick up the sun in pieces small
To store them in my blue jeans’ pocket,
Knitting up lint of mine in miniature
On a rock of clay doing the grand tour.
Desire is known as a field of weeds -
Only ever a model of nature’s beauty.
And posing on a lone hill outside my window,
A lone light-bulb filters my mind
With eyes closed to the leaves of time,
Which downward falls in a’ near-rhyme.

title: Untitled (Italian Actress)
publication: Published in Virginia Writers Project in 2026
body: I want to know an Italian actress of days
gone by,
someone of the stage who acted plays
In a dialect we no longer have
much access to --
Not really.
Of whom the role was written for -- a shining
star
in the twilight of a dying civilization,
who sang her songs wordlessly, but hit all
the high notes,
who embodied the corpse of a once great
Providence,
a divinity coughing in between the set
pieces,
who remained a name
in a book of games and therefore an
enigma
or something for the humanity I know but
you know not,
yet was once played out repeatedly as an answer.

title: Upon August’s Slumped Back
publication: Published in Duane’s Poe Tree in 2020
body: Upon August’s slumped back
the weight of the previous year
bends his crooked spine
with tender years.
And with this timely scoliosis,
his abject form
welcomes the wind unassuming,
a midnight guest
wandering like a mischievous child,
who comes to steal
what it wills
as the household goes off to bed,
windows open,
with a peace of being from nature’s massage;
and as in a bag,
my thoughts westward go,
like this fickle air,
to the drawn map’s end;
nobody knows
of the wind wrapped round
my pinky finger.
I hold it so tightly,
but now let it go, never to linger,
ever to dance with Astraeus,
as with a stranger sans affection.
For in this season,
the coffers are packed to the brim
with rare objects and predictions grim,
such are
conversations with my friend,
my mind,
in these confines
the size
of a mumble,
spanking the new-born hours into a cry
to wake the turn of Seasons,
who die.
The night’s cold has passing silent
escaped
like wards of a jail
for familial violence;
seasons, like the rejected bit of a song,
kill the following strain --
with strain in strain and by strain.
It’s a pledge to the darkness
of time fallen
outside our doors.

title: Valentine
body: a heart, not so very distant
a heart, not so very distant
a heart, not so very distant
a heart not so very distant
a heart, NOT so very distant
a heart, not so very distant
a heart, not so very distant…

title: Verse that wants to be a Prose poem
body: Man says, “in the real world…”
as soon as I brought up some ideal,
some principle of the philosophic –
or practical life.  As in: Practice, n.:
The act of thinking before you speak.
His lips betrayed himself,
curling to indicate some pride
as if at thirty fucking five,
he’s proud of recognizing reality.
Jesus.  The real world –
shoot me. For any obscenity
is more poetic than this phrase
(and if you can’t recognize
that poetry is swearing –
you have no oath to give).
The next thing you’ll say is –
‘nothing lasts forever.’ Uh-huh…
But if the matter of physics says
nothing can be created nor destroyed,
then, in essence –
Everything actually lasts forever.
(Except for metaphors).
Any – way, any real way…
“the real world.” You say what I should think,
being more proud of the words
put in my mouth
than the ones put in yours.
This is the practice of idiots
--of idiots who don’t practice
but take a swing at empty air
and call themselves prodigies
of the pedestrian ennui –
(which is rarely interesting
…and never unique).
Man says a word,
and it bores the hell out of me.

title: Wagner at the Opera
body: Prelude
F
Night after night, at a lamppost’s height
Euterpe’s charge in an armadillo shell,
closed in a cavern of ethereal might,
a hurricane of sound swells --
Did you take such a breath?
Indoors,
we gel to the music, of the indoor swirl
(like a toilet bowl).
B
What to find, but a Lazarus of mind
Fueling ideas of an extinct kind
D#
As I hold my sign of protest, I know
‘euphemism’ is a euphemism.
From the mouth of the Goebbels of atheists flow
Words.  They are ours (a refraction – prismatic),
and all along every inch of the fret move,
piping aqua vitae to the Holy Land’s summit
G#
A day a day
(for the sum total of nothing: "eine Handlung”)
The seated took it.  An aesthetic
dossier of ear-ale drunk but not drunken.
For him, the past is a screen that mocks ignorance, and
I see relics of a present that could have been:
season of
trysts and colds (oh, Valkyries of Time
die so an epic may play again).
War didn’t begin here.
Just the absence of harmony.
Act 1
F
‘Wild Irish Maid’s’
--only exist on the tongues of those who
tell tales.  On every helm
is a sailor of the coming day,
while the North Atlantic sea
moves like a laugh
across the face of the earth.
“I would it were rising to consume us.”
B
She found him like she left him,
which is the story of a’ ‘mortally wounded’ life
D#
(And a wedding march is)
played by a percussion of feet only -- walking
down aisles of the temporal,
the church was a fermentable sea,
of cherubs n’ babes weeping ‘Morold,’
and one-handed claps.
G#
Hand in hand with a weary traveler,
the Flying Dutchman portents
the lower depth’s king,
who wears a crown of albatrosses,
seagulls and cloud surfers -- king to horrors sugarcoated.
Look into the eyes; she can’t kill him
Look into the eyes; the gloss is truth.
In your eyes, would
I fall in hate of you?
Then, Kurwenal, the middle, will not contend
a love made of brew – to not offend.
Act 2
F
‘Too late – ‘
comes round the halls a Wallpaper voice
to decorate the house of many rooms.
Crowds like booze fill too many holes.
In moist outdoors
a logorrhea
of minutes dance by in a reverbed churn,
burning wills into a Neo-Grecian urn
B
Violence is the motif…for society is
when dogs hunt for another party.
D#
(The point is I want
what I shouldn’t want
I want
to not want because of the
point that I cannot want
want)…But this world is nothing but premonition.
G#
But hush --
‘I exhaust my flame,’ like
friends and funds.
Marke the flame.  Marke the dame.
In a bedchamber – synonyms not lost for:
‘chamber’ -- hearts syncopate.
Their limbs only indicate
to new men on, drawn back to the castle.
And so nothing discovered all: in coitus,
spying eyes
raise up the sun to a height it’s afraid of.
Act 3
F
Now, a chord of wind rents the sky --
a hasty scrawled rest:
mimicry of a babe’s haunting cry,
who at a mother’s young breast
suckles the memory of fat-free milk.
The rooster that caws
in a tender valley of noon,
notes the rod but not the staff.
B
So pipes eat themselves, in an Ouroboros
when leitmotifs are leitmotifs.
D#
“I know this song…”
The lover’s delirium walks with clenched hands --
remove
Melot’s signature on vellum new,
remove feet to talk in a sign language
of heels.  Or tears.
G#
Reign of obsequy in a sequined dress --
musical notes battle like a game of chess,
awoke a queen of too tender
thoughts, bought with a coupon: gratis,
A nubile with a lipstick imprints
He died.
she was of legal age for the apocalypse,
(But oh, Marke explained the poison n’ words)
(But oh, mark how sad ‘tis when your name
is synonymous with ‘goodbye’)
Finale
F
On stage, a field of crosses knits the ground’s spouse
who’s only grounds-kept
by a field mouse.
And mourners of weeds, brambles, and briers --
for nothing is nothing in shambles perspired --
form suits so primped and pressed
for a marriage in death, for who
dare not walk ‘neath Jacob’s ladder.
B
If an audience is those who watch,
can an audience but obey?
D#
For Jacob’s ladder is a stairway to nothing
to the German watching himself at a play.
Should he cry, he cries for he,
so say tea leaves with the motto of
“anything in wolves’ clothing
Is probably a sheep.”
G#
The sour aftertaste of false idols
is like a morning kiss -- of lovers twixt.
Glossolalia
should sound like a scratched record --
a bohemian groan spit from a phonograph’s
propaganda.
Wagner sits counting the silences of his musical until
“Liebstod,”
as earthbound
as a twice-born bird
we’re separated from the herd.
And there is where redemption lies.

title: Walk Away, Walk Away
body: I thought he watched me walk away,
ending meaning in a line,
and only found meaning in the
movement
of these (hips --
just like only finding meaning in said line)
breaks.
It was his one failing
Among all the others…

title: Waterfall
publication: Published in Artvilla, poetry life and times in 2018 / Republished in Ink Pantry around 2018
body: I want my thoughts
to descend
like a waterfall,
such that the droplets form
an image of you.

title: Westerplatte, Gdansk
publication: Published in DoveTales, Writing for Peace in 2019
body: Walked along a sea that never changes,
a sea that in the midst of the night
tells a lie to everyone who looks into it,
a sea whose harbor knows its shame.
The world was watching as this port
twisted the truth with a stoic lapping,
providing a misguided quote that
covered for a bomb that blew up the world.

title: What Poets Think About in the Dark When No One’s There…
publication: Published in Chewers by Masticadores in 2026
body: Poets love to write about shit they know nothing about.
But they hide that fact behind a sloppy line break.
They stack words together like refugees
canned into a space too small for them.
That’s probably too much, which – excess --
is something poets claim they don’t do,
when all poetry depends on excess, i.e.
the strange proliferation of lecherous words.
I’d allude to Mallarme if I believed you read him
(or at least stumbled through his verbal marsh).
Oh, to make you fall into a tiny death,
to tickle your fancy until you laugh your life away.
This is a poem I wore for myself -- full coverage,
but I expect you to be a voyeur and look through it.
Meanwhile, I’d carve your name on a bar stool
like fools do on the naked torsos of trees.
Only this etch marks who you feel
envy for the most, for this round’s never
on me, because it’s ultimately the fattest lips
that say the darned kindest things.
Sometimes we find our philosophy
written on the bottom of a bottle,
after the world has slipped
into a soft oblivion. Excess:
How I’d dance on this floor,
to some music that is never played,
when the dark has come to tuck in
the children of this plight.
I smoked my fingers with a lit cigarette
into the ember of a religion of old -- brutalized
by the very evils of the new boss.  Can’t you see
how all things are the same? -- I don’t even try.

title: When I See a Smirk
publication: Published in Neologism in 2013-2018. / Republished in Ginosko in 2026
body: When I see a smirk flutter ‘cross your face
I try to follow it with mil’tant gaze.
Shall I see it upon your cheek in chase?
Or will it be but a’ sly, imagined haze?
Or perhaps your lips with a gentle crease
Will tell me what you keep under lock n’ key -
The fine lines of some kiss-in-waiting free
Those lines from out of which you try to cease.
Might your hand reveal with nervous jitter,
Palsy out with a’ twitter, th’ secret you keep -
While butterflies bred of numbrous litter
Are caged behind your fat windows ev’r deep.
So in a marathon of sight I sprint
In mirth, to find some shy and living hint.

title: When…
publication: Published in Artvilla, poetry life and times in 2018 / Republished in Ink Pantry around 2018
body: When every word you’ve used
Too much --
It’s a hollowed word,
Sans thought.

title: Widow
body: She dropped everything to become a wife,
And to take that honorable title.
To scrawl “Mrs.” unto a foreign life,
Now her own, now her letters hyetal.
Dropping the world else for commitment aught,
She’d picture themselves one day cotching old
In winter; and starve the present to naught
But stories to look back on and be told.
Her hand entangled in her husband’s ret,
She thought it selfless to suffer abuse --
Her hand always out of her own pocket.
She thought it moral to excuse her use.
And then he died, and she was not a wife.
She was just a word colored in by strife.

title: Wink
body: For with your eyes shut
you become disembodied,
what Redon calls,
“the strange harm of closed eyes.”
You evolve in this darkness,
into a play of flirtation
from the eye,
a chiaroscuro with the light.
We all r-evolve around our traumas,
taken two ways
(a phrase taken two ways that is)
to become ourselves.
You print your mad dreams
on those two paper lids,
as fair as an adjective
dangling upon the familiar --
Familiar like your face,
a polyp of mystery,
which somewhere else
lies in material being.
But in my mind,
it fosters a feeling --
one felt with the eye,
one felt with a prick
from behind that selenian sty.

title: Winter
body: Amidst of some sort of witch's hour,
I've wrestled with my pillow dour --
(Isn’t it odd how the sun’s rind,
tricks you when you’re trying to be so kind?)
As that cruel jester mocks me so near
how does it know my secrets -- my fear?
I can picture his face from dots of snow
(And I see it a 'him' counting between the au).
Dali said the sexiest part of a woman
was her secrets.  So I know in syn’nym
the blinding snowflakes grow larger northerly bent,
feeding off my ever-falling discontent.
(everyone remembers that Shakespeare line,
but they forget the following, entwined:
"Made glorious summer by this sun of York."
But none there is, when Höðr the sun does cork).

title: Winter Afternoon
body: I am writing a poem because it’s winter,
and I am inside.  I don’t want to
Right now, and
it shows –
“Proving” my point by showing this poor muddle --
better than the telling words,
flowery as they could be,
tattling in their own way,
and reveling in my own circle of complaints.

title: Winter Song
body: I think our feet are dragging us down,
and we all wish we lived in California,
but I've been blown out by a melted candle
and already your voice is so warm.
So when the cowardly sun hides himself
I'll be young again -- and we'll
go inside to wander, intransitive verb,
get lost in our home’s pen.
But this house has always been shrinking
because winter comes on too fast.
And I only wish that everything were temperate
as you’ve already driven past.

title: Word Map of a Cat on a Mat
publication: Published in Artvilla, poetry life and times in 2018 / Republished in Ink Pantry around 2018
body: Putting the indexes out,
I saw the cat,
Sleeping with torso outstretched
While I, unheimlich, rushed to and fro;
On a mat, it sat -- in peace,
And I said sighing, what I want is that.

title: Writing Abuse
publication: Published in Pilcrow and Dagger in 2018
body: Beat me to the floor again,
for I spend more time licking the linoleum,
than mopping up my sloppy words.
It was a long time coming
but a longer time gone --
because even dumb words cry loudly
when uttered by the heart.
We don’t talk about things;
we only put them down into paragraphs.
Holding opinions
Min turns the word over on the page,
with a snap --
and I’m put back into a shack,
a hold not big enough to contain these emotions.
Our highs move laws meet to meet,
so it happens again…
“My love” – the word has abused me again.
Yet again.
Why do I write? What delirium to me unknown
dips this venereal quill --
and then brings the tip to hone?
I don’t know.
This desk’s like a roundtable for two,
and in this pas de deux
I wanted to sit as far away from myself
as possible,
but there wasn’t a chair,
so in my idleness
I become a recidivist of masochism.
The ink sinks its teeth into my skin,
and its poison spreads again –
I go back to the trace of words
that call me ‘fool’ and me do gird.
There’s tremors in my hand,
and similar likeness in my mind.
And in this nisus
of slow death passing,
this surly pen
talks back to me more than I can talk for myself.
A dilettanti
of self-abuse,
I am such as the pen is to paper,
abnegating its connection to the mind.
I cannot escape my abusive lover:
Me, drooling with a baby’s spittle,
trying to hobble the long road away
to a heart fickle
(and talking to an audience).
It’s like forming a love triangle with the therapist.

title: You remind me of somebody that I never met
body: As Nadja said, “with the end of my breath,
which is the beginning of yours.”
I felt enraptured with those spaces,
those sudden intervals between breaks
in the words we perpetually speak.
Ne’er spoken to you, but tattooed
on my tongue as if some
hiraeth for a strange desire.
I fell into the present with a bang,
the world else nothing but an elison,
the only sound that of your name.
I fell into this space, forever reading
that which was not there
where I get stuck in your words –
“you remind me of somebody
that I never met.” But words
can’t even come out of my mouth
and fall into this humble verse
because it wouldn’t be as perfect
as this fleeting moment is.

title: You were but I was (A sonnet inspired poem)
publication: Published in North of Oxford in 2018ish? / Republished in Feed the Holy OR Masticadores USA in 2026
body: The day was exhausted, as much were we.
When you said those words, you said them with teeth.
looking within me, eyes minatory.
I peered instead at your tone underneath.
Were I to charge, a fee placed on ego,
my throat, a prisoner, wouldn’t react:
You aimed directly at my morillo
to stop those quite words right in their tracks.
The War of the Roses entered act two:
to make me cow to your vile rhetoric,
all those castrating winds, to me, you blew
What am I? Selfish, immature, a dick?
Beside the lonely road, where no movement
Is allowed, ‘cept my heart invisible
Our car pavisanding, its wax lucent,
With a wheel stuck for greater principles
You said you were kidding – spoke in a buzz,
that I wasn’t that.  You were but I was.

title: You've Stolen the East
body: And all along the Scottish moors,
you've tied a word to your tongue
And kept it like a little pet.
For all the mother's words undone
(damn you!)
how well can I know it
when it's only under the foot of you?
If I could blacken my eyes,
and bury my ear,
and if I succumb to mortality’s airs,
I am going to yell at my face
throughout the longest period of a breath --
a punctuation on Lethe.
But the Spring's aria,
it sings of you.
You've stolen the east.
You've stolen the west.
And now, for all there is --
only is, through the window of you.
And the external world is emaciated
into a skeletal boon.
And I fear, in this amour--
you've stolen my spirit too.
My memories become a statue --
sculpted with an arthritic hand,
a stranger unto myself.
And all that I see is yet to be.

title: Zelda; Or Everything I Needed to Learn About Economics
publication: Published in Call me [Brackets] in 2020 / Republished in Feed the Holy OR Masticadores USA in 2026
body: A plenum of air
is all that you own --
until you’re smacking through your neighbor’s flower pots,
collecting rupees for some quest or not.
The open land of Hyrule,
a monarchic kingdom,
is a reliquary of delirium
that requires you to collect all you can,
For holding onto things indefinitely
is the nature of economy,
and we could all buy any single item,
given the understanding we never need eat, rest, or sleep.
Green is the color of tave,
Of money, heroes, him --
In a fantasy world where “and to save”
Is a bitter contronym.
So you trim the grass for a rupee,
carrying more items than possible --
and then once you have those,
it’s easier to get more,
Until you own clothes for the part
when no one else owns a second pair,
and it requires some evil imbroglio
For you to be the chosen one here
Because you’re always one more link in a chain
of a long economic fetter,
in which history repeats itself painfully
with the same evil rising anon,
Until someone writes the happy ending --
The people, they may fall,
but the kingdom never did.
You’re always the hero as a kid.
